The notch is just the nicest place for it, not the only one. On a Mac without a notch (or with the lid closed on an external display), Termy skips the notch and moves everything to the menu bar: the icon changes color when an agent needs you, approval notifications have Allow / Deny buttons right on them, and the panel drops down from the menu bar on whichever screen you're using, with the same approval banner. If your MacBook is open next to the monitor, the notch keeps working on the laptop screen.

Your AI coding agent can get a new feature working perfectly and still hand back a fundamentally broken codebase. In HumanLayer's October 2026 SlopCodeBench run, Claude Opus 5.5 at medium reasoning effort implemented the requested feature on 145 out of 196 checkpoints—but kept the overall application strictly working on only 28.

Why does autonomous AI code rot so quickly over time? [...] [12:48] old tests are where it opened. When your agent's code starts to rot, which shows up first for you, broken old features or new code growing sideways.
